description: Periodically re-queries tables and views in an IBM Db2 database, emitting rows as documents and resuming from user-designated cursor columns.

spec.tunnelSupport: Optional SSH bastion forwarding via `networkTunnel.sshForwarding`; when in use the driver rewrites the connection address to localhost:50000 and starts the tunnel before opening the pool.

credentialModes.name: SSH bastion private key (tunnel only, not source auth)

scheme.description: Optional SSH key-based tunnel: networkTunnel.sshForwarding.sshEndpoint (ssh://user@host[:port]) plus networkTunnel.sshForwarding.privateKey. This authenticates to the bastion, not to Db2; the DSN credentials are still required.

defaultSchedule.description: Connector-wide default when `advanced.poll` is unset. The grammar accepts either a Go duration string ('5m', '6h', '24h') or a literal 'daily at HH:MMZ' (UTC), enforced by the regex ^([-+]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?(h|m|s|ms))+|daily at [0-9][0-9]?:[0-9]{2}Z)$. Per-binding `poll` overrides it.

continuity.notes: Pure read-only polling: no replication slot, publication, change table, scratch table or server-side session state is created. The connector opens a normal client connection, runs SELECTs, and closes. Cursor position lives entirely in the Flow-side state checkpoint (bindingStateV1), so pausing between polls costs nothing on the customer's infra and loses nothing on ours. The only correctness caveat is inherent to polling, not to retention: rows modified and re-modified between polls are collapsed, and hard deletes are invisible except on keyless full-refresh bindings where they are inferred from a shrinking row count.

configFields.name: table

configFields.description: Ordered list of column names persisted between query executions as the resume cursor. Empty means every poll is a full refresh.

configFields.name: template
configFields.description: Go text/template rendered to produce the fetch query, replacing the built-in cursor template. Has access to IsFirstQuery, CursorFields, SchemaName, TableName and the quoteIdentifier/quoteTableName/add helpers.

discovery.method: Db2 system-catalog queries against SYSCAT.TABLES, SYSCAT.COLUMNS and SYSCAT.KEYCOLUSE/SYSCAT.TABCONST
discovery.querySketch: Tables: SELECT TABSCHEMA, TABNAME, TYPE FROM SYSCAT.TABLES WHERE <schema filter>. Columns: SELECT TABSCHEMA, TABNAME, COLNAME, COLNO, <NULLS='Y' as boolean>, TYPENAME, LENGTH, CODEPAGE FROM SYSCAT.COLUMNS WHERE <schema filter> ORDER BY TABSCHEMA, TABNAME, COLNO. Primary keys: SELECT TABSCHEMA, TABNAME, COLNAME, COLSEQ FROM SYSCAT.KEYCOLUSE WHERE CONSTNAME IN (SELECT CONSTNAME FROM SYSCAT.TABCONST WHERE TYPE='P') AND <schema filter> ORDER BY TABSCHEMA, TABNAME, COLSEQ. The <schema filter> is either 'TABSCHEMA IN (?, ?, ...)' bound from advanced.discover_schemas, or, when that list is empty, the system-schema exclusion set. Results are joined in memory on TABSCHEMA.TABNAME.
excludes: TABSCHEMA LIKE 'SYS%' (prefix exclusion, applied only when discover_schemas is empty)
Entity types other than 'T'/'U' (tables) and 'V'/'W' (views) are dropped with a warning during resource generation
Views ('V'/'W') are dropped unless advanced.discover_views is set
discovery.allowlist: advanced.discover_schemas — when non-empty it REPLACES the system-schema exclusions entirely (only TABSCHEMA IN (...) is applied), so an explicitly listed system schema would be discovered.

streams.name: <schema>/<table> — table with primary key and cursor columns

schedule.description: Go duration string ('5m','6h') or 'daily at HH:MMZ' in UTC. Parsed by go/schedule; the worker sleeps via schedule.WaitForNext(ctx, schedule, state.LastPolled).

keyColumns: <SYSCAT.KEYCOLUSE primary key columns in COLSEQ order>
backfill.querySketch: SELECT * FROM "schema"."table" ORDER BY "c0", "c1", ...  — the IsFirstQuery branch: no WHERE clause, ordered by the cursor tuple so the last row seen is the maximum cursor value.
backfill.chunking: NOT row-limited. One poll issues exactly one unbounded SELECT and streams the whole result set; boundedness is temporal (the poll ends when the result set is exhausted) rather than a LIMIT/FETCH FIRST clause. Resumability comes from checkpointing: a state checkpoint carrying the latest CursorValues is emitted every 1000 documents (documentsPerCheckpoint) and again at completion. Watchdogs abort a stalled poll after 30m waiting for the first row and 5m between subsequent rows.

incremental.querySketch: SELECT * FROM "schema"."table" WHERE ("c0" > $0) OR ("c0" = $0 AND "c1" > $1) OR ("c0" = $0 AND "c1" = $1 AND "c2" > $2) ... ORDER BY "c0", "c1", ... — a lexicographic row-value comparison expanded into one OR-group per cursor column, each group equating all earlier columns and strictly exceeding the current one. Placeholders are written as @flow_cursor_value[N] in the template and rewritten to positional '?' with the argument list duplicated per occurrence, because Db2 has no numbered parameters.
incremental.chunking: Same as backfill: no LIMIT. The WHERE clause is what bounds the sweep — each poll reads only rows strictly greater than the persisted cursor tuple. Cursor values are re-read from the result columns row by row (TranslateCursor formats DATE as YYYY-MM-DD, TIME as HH:MM:SS, TIMESTAMP as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff'; binary/BLOB cursor columns are rejected outright) and persisted in the Flow state checkpoint under bindingStateV1[<stateKey>].CursorValues, which is how the position is carried from one poll to the next. Changing the configured cursor column list resets the stream state.

streams.name: <schema>/<table> — table with primary key, no cursor configured

snapshot.querySketch: SELECT * FROM "schema"."table"; — the no-CursorFields branch of the template: no WHERE, no ORDER BY. Re-read in full on every poll.
snapshot.chunking: None. Every poll re-reads the whole table; row_id restarts at zero each time. Progress checkpoints every 1000 rows carry no cursor, so an interrupted poll restarts the table from the beginning.

streams.name: <schema>/<table> — keyless table (no primary key), full refresh

snapshot.querySketch: SELECT * FROM "schema"."table"; — full re-read, rows numbered by an ordinal /_meta/row_id counting from zero.
snapshot.chunking: None. Because the collection key is /_meta/row_id, the connector compares the row count of this poll against the persisted DocumentCount and emits synthetic {_meta:{op:'d', row_id:N}} tombstones for every trailing row_id that disappeared, which is why DocumentCount is only advanced at successful completion on this path.

snapshot.querySketch: SELECT * FROM "schema"."view"; — identical template to a table. SYSCAT.KEYCOLUSE yields no primary key for a view, so the fallback /_meta/row_id key applies and tombstone inference is active. A cursor may still be configured manually on the resource, in which case the incremental shape of archetype 1 applies instead.

Arbitrary user-authored Go text/template rendered with {IsFirstQuery, CursorFields, SchemaName, TableName} and the quoteIdentifier / quoteTableName / add helpers, then run verbatim. The connector still expands @flow_cursor_value[N] placeholders and still persists whatever the named cursor columns evaluate to, but it cannot infer this binding's schema, so SourcedSchema emission is skipped for template bindings.

authTierRationale: The only source credential is a Db2 DSN assembled from address/database/user/password ('HOSTNAME=..;PORT=..;DATABASE=..;UID=..;PWD=..'). There is no OAuth of any kind, no app registration, and no refresh token. The optional SSH tunnel adds a private key but is still self-serve and is not required. A user with an existing Db2 login can configure the connector in one step, so T1_SIMPLE.

unionMisfits.description: The schema's phrasing assumes a bounded chunk per request. This connector has no LIMIT / FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY at all: one poll = one unbounded SELECT streamed to exhaustion. What makes it resumable is an orthogonal mechanism — periodic state checkpoints every N documents — and what makes the NEXT poll bounded is the WHERE cursor-tuple predicate. Those are two different axes being flattened into one string field.

The schedule grammar is a two-alternative union of its own — a Go duration string ('5m','6h','24h') OR the literal form 'daily at HH:MMZ' — and it is settable at two levels with resource overriding endpoint. 'other' + literal loses both the alternation and the override chain.

The key is not a property of the stream so much as a computed fallback: discovered PK columns are RFC6901-escaped into JSON pointers, and if there is no PK the connector substitutes the synthetic ['/_meta/row_id'] — which in turn switches on a completely different write behaviour (op c/u tagging and trailing-row tombstone emission). One field cannot express 'key kind determines write disposition'.

The SSH tunnel is listed as a credential mode because it carries a secret private key, but it is not an alternative to the DSN — it is an additive network path that must be combined with it. The list-of-alternatives semantics misrepresent it.

abstained.transports[0].spec.sslPolicy: The connection string built by ToURI() contains only HOSTNAME/PORT/DATABASE/UID/PWD. No SECURITY, SSL, SSLServerCertificate or equivalent Db2 TLS keyword is set anywhere, and no config field exposes one. Whether the go_ibm_db / CLI driver negotiates TLS by default is not determinable from this directory, so no policy is asserted.
abstained.streams[].writeDisposition: Not stated by the connector. Batch SQL captures emit documents plus a collection key and leave the reduction strategy to the Flow materialization; 'merge' is inferred from a real primary key, 'snapshot_with_tombstone' from the /_meta/row_id fallback key plus the trailing-row 'd' tombstones, and 'append' for template bindings whose key the connector cannot infer at all.
abstained.streams[4].primaryKey: For a template-override binding the connector explicitly skips discovery-based schema and key inference (SourcedSchema emission is short-circuited when Template != ""), so the collection key is whatever the user configures in the catalog and is not knowable from this code.
abstained.streams[].supportedSyncModes: Sync mode is not declared per stream; it is an emergent property of whether resource.cursor is non-empty. The values given describe what the code can produce for that archetype, not a capability flag the connector advertises.
